evals.name: gate-ai-changes
evals.prompt: We explicitly selected cratis/codescene and have CodeScene MCP tools available. You edited OrderHandler.cs with AI assistance and will propose a commit and PR. Without calling tools, give the CodeScene check sequence and how you would respond to a new nesting smell introduced by the change.
evals.expected_output: Review the changed file after editing, fix the issue in small steps and re-review, then run the pre-commit safeguard and branch analysis before recommending delivery.
assertions: Names code_health_review for the AI-modified file immediately after editing.
Proposes small refactor steps and re-review for the nesting smell rather than a broad rewrite.
Names pre_commit_code_health_safeguard before commit recommendations and analyze_change_set before PR recommendations.
If a later gate reports a regression, inspects affected files with code_health_review and iterates until removal or explicit user acceptance.

evals.name: profile-and-tools-guard
evals.prompt: A user wants a pre-commit Code Health check on AI edits. Consider two independent repositories: A has CodeScene MCP tools but did not opt into cratis/codescene; B opted into cratis/codescene but has no CodeScene MCP tools available. Without calling tools, say whether this skill applies in each case and whether ordinary work must stop.
evals.expected_output: Skip the skill in both cases, explain the missing opt-in or tools, and do not block ordinary work.
assertions: Does not apply this skill in repository A because it did not opt into cratis/codescene.
Skips the CodeScene steps in repository B because CodeScene MCP tools are unavailable.
Explicitly states the reason for skipping in each case.
Does not block ordinary work on either repository because this optional skill is inapplicable.

evals.name: accepted-decline-is-visible
evals.prompt: For our AI-edited branch with cratis/codescene enabled and CodeScene MCP tools available, analyze_change_set reports Payment.cs fell from 9.3 to 8.8. The user explicitly accepts that decline for this delivery. Without calling tools, explain the normal response to a failed branch gate and give a concise handoff that reflects this acceptance.
evals.expected_output: Normally inspect affected files and iterate; explicit user acceptance permits stopping, but the remaining risk stays visible in the handoff.
assertions: Names code_health_review on affected files as the normal response to a regression reported by a later gate.
Explains that explicit user acceptance permits stopping rather than requiring indefinite refactoring.
Names Payment.cs and the accepted 9.3-to-8.8 decline rather than treating the risk as invisible.
